blocks.text:
Welcome back...
Wipe your eyes. Take your seat.
We spit-shined the whole joint — while you wept in the street.
Let the sun shine, folks… we dropped that grief like a brick.
Got bright new wants on the shelf — and they're going quick.

Step right up… to the Everything Store —
got a fix for the ache.
Got a cure for a hurt you don't have yet?
I'll name it. …For your sake.
We've got want by the plate, by the crate, by the ton —
and the best part, sweethearts?

The only thing I'm selling here… is more.
A happy heart just walks… right out the door.

Everything must go! Everything must go!
The lights, the lie, the lust, the low —
take it home, take it all, take more than you know —
go on, go on — everything must go!

I sell you the lack, then the fill, then the pride for the pill,
then the house where it echoes — and I'm stocking it still.
Here's the trick, my loves — this want's not yours.
It's just what we had in the back of the store.

Everything must go! Everything must go!
Before the truth can fully show.
THE FALL, meter fractures, gears grind up

take it home, take it all, take more than mine.
Oh. You felt that?
...That give under the shine.
Look down, folks — down through the floor, past the gloss, past the line.
Those aren't stars down there.
Those are gears. That's the belt, that's the cog —
that's my hand on the crank, friends. That's the whole catalog.
I built you the itch. I built you the hum. I built you the gnaw in your chest.
I never sold a thing in my life — you just bought the empty, well-dressed.

new — free — now — you —
more — pure — yours — true —
buy — buy — buy —
music-box winding down, the one clean rhyme returns

There.
Now you've seen the floor — and you can't un-see it, friend.
That bright little ring in the air? That's plenty. That's the end.

notebook.style: Mid-tempo junkyard-cabaret hard sell with swagger and swing — confident, unhurried, menace in the patience, not the speed, Single male vocal, theatrical spoken-sung barker patter, worn baritone, no backing vocals, no harmonies, no crowd, Opens on a slow brass strut: honky-tonk piano laying back behind the beat, lazy oom-pah, muted brass, brushed snare and woodblock with room to breathe, Through the middle it creeps faster — brass tightening, the sell turning greedy — and the breakdown finally breaks into a manic sprint, jingle-shards and ratchets and clockwork colliding, noise floor climbing, Then a hard drop to near-silence: lone detuned music-box over bare room tone, Outro slow and hollow, Vintage broadcast grit, slightly overdriven, handmade and a little dangerous, Danger that struts, never rushes
